harness: MainActivity (foreground Activity) + adb shell dumpsys polling
measurement_method: adb shell dumpsys meminfo/thermalservice/battery polled every 15s — NO code changes to harness, purely external observation
rounds_completed: 2 full-corpus runs completed + round 3 partially observed (NNAPI provider still running when data collection stopped) — 20.6 minutes total observation time with relaunch pauses between rounds

ram_pss_kb.note: PSS peaks ~910MB during NNAPI provider; ~650-670MB during CPU/XNNPACK. Matches known per-graph RSS profile: vector_estimator.onnx alone loads ~150MB RSS (see §0.2 per-graph RSS on macOS host)

skin_temp_c.trend: Rises during continuous benchmark (peak 50.6°C), cools between rounds (drops to ~46°C when app restarts)

thermal.cpu_temp_c_note: Sensor reports constant 88.512°C across all samples — likely a cached/stale or max-value sensor reading on this OnePlus device. Not reliable as a trend indicator. Use SKIN temp for trend analysis.

thermal_status.trend: Starts at 0 (NONE), escalates to 1 (LIGHT) within ~2min of continuous load, reaches 3 (SEVERE) by ~4min, stays at 3 during sustained load. Drops back to 2 when app pauses between rounds. Never reaches 4 (CRITICAL).

battery.note: Device was charging (PlugType=2=USB) during measurement. Battery drain rate may differ when unplugged. Temperature rose from 350 to ~422 (units: dsi, /10 = 35.0→42.2°C).

what_this_proves: First-ever on-device RAM (PSS/RSS) and thermal/battery measurements for the v3 Nano mobile harness. PSS peaks at ~910MB during NNAPI load (consistent with per-graph RSS profile: vector_estimator.onnx alone loads ~150MB). Thermal escalates to SEVERE (PowerManager.THERMAL_STATUS=3) within ~4 minutes of continuous full-corpus benchmarking but never reaches CRITICAL (4). Skin temperature rises ~6°C over continuous load (44→50.6°C) and cools to ~46°C during brief idle pauses between rounds. Battery drain 5% over 20.6 minutes (~15%/hour) while charging — real drain rate when unplugged would be higher. Peak RSS ~1.09GB on device (vs 476MB peak RSS on macOS host — significant difference due to NNAPI provider loading additional buffers + Android process overhead).
what_this_does_NOT_prove: NOT a full 30-60 minute soak test per protocol 002 §H8 — this is a ~20-minute short soak with relaunch pauses between rounds. RTF degradation under thermal throttle not measured (would need RTF data correlated with thermal status over time). Only 1 Android device (OnePlus PHP110). iOS has no equivalent external measurement method without code changes. CPU temperature sensor reports constant value (unreliable for trend). Battery was charging during test.
